title: Embodied Interpretability: Linking Causal Understanding to Generalization in Vision-Language-Action Models
models: pi0.5 (fine-tuned from pi05 base on AGNOSTOS seen tasks, RLBench Franka)
methods: Interventional Significance Score (ISS): RISE-style Monte Carlo Bernoulli masking with Gaussian-blur mixing, action L2 change as proxy for KL divergence
Nuisance Mass Ratio (NMR): share of top-k% ISS saliency falling on segmented nuisance regions
robustness and fidelity tests with soft (noise) and hard (texture, geometric, patch) interventions on nuisance regions
theory: unbiasedness and conditions for action error as divergence proxy
question: Can an interventional visual attribution score tell whether a VLA relies on task-relevant or nuisance regions, and does nuisance reliance predict generalization?
key_findings: Task-level NMR@10 correlates with closed-loop success rate at r = -0.77 (41 AGNOSTOS tasks x 5 seeds, 25 trials each); k = 10 was chosen because it gave the strongest correlation among k in {1, 5, 10, 15, 20}.

Fidelity: correlation between saliency change and action change under texture / geometric / patch perturbations of nuisance regions is r = 0.78 / 0.64 / 0.72 for ISS vs 0.64 / 0.49 / 0.56 for attention and 0.47 / 0.33 / 0.40 for token norm; on unseen geometric perturbations ISS r = 0.79 vs 0.60 (ATT) and 0.48 (NORM).
Robustness to Gaussian noise in nuisance regions (200 episodes): ISS saliency cosine 0.995 with action MSE 0.002, attention 0.959, token norm 0.999 (with higher action MSE 0.011).
Wrist view attributions stay on manipulation-relevant parts (nuisance ratio 0.02-0.15) while front (0.24-0.56) and overhead (0.21-0.38) views spread to robot links and background.
pi0.5 success after fine-tuning: 59.07 +/- 0.58% on seen tasks, 24.00 +/- 1.92% on unseen (28.74% level-1, 16.96% level-2).
ISS cost: N = 100 masks, about 5.18 s per explanation (0.19 Hz), so offline only.

evidence.setting: simulation (RLBench via AGNOSTOS) for success rates; ISS/NMR computed offline on dataset episodes
benchmarks: AGNOSTOS (18 seen, 13 unseen level-1, 10 unseen level-2 tasks) in RLBench
evidence.scale: 3,600 training episodes, 575 unseen evaluation episodes; success over 5 seeds x 41 tasks x 25 trials; fidelity on 1,000 sampled episodes; robustness on 200 episodes
evidence.statistics: partial: Pearson correlations and mean +/- SD over seeds; no CIs on the correlations, no control for task split

causal_validation: At the input level only: ISS is defined by masking interventions and its fidelity is checked against perturbation-induced action changes. There is no intervention showing that reducing nuisance reliance improves generalization; the NMR-generalization link is correlational.
closed_loop: Success rates are closed-loop (RLBench); attribution and fidelity analyses are open-loop on single-step predictions under teacher forcing.
limitations_stated: Assumes a unimodal action distribution so that action error is a valid proxy for divergence.
Monte Carlo cost restricts ISS to offline analysis.
NMR depends on nuisance segmentation masks, which are costly and error-prone in the real world.
critique: The headline r = -0.77 pools seen and unseen tasks; seen tasks have both higher success and plausibly lower nuisance attribution, so the correlation may mostly separate the two splits. A within-split correlation or a regression controlling for split is needed; k was also chosen to maximize r.
Points from the 5 seeds of the same task are not independent, which inflates the apparent sample size behind r.

Flow-matching pi0.5 has stochastic, potentially multimodal outputs, the case the authors flag as violating their unimodality assumption; how noise is fixed across masked passes is not clear in the text read.
It is input saliency, not mechanistic interpretability despite the framing; the comparison against attention maps is useful because many VLA papers rely on attention as explanation.
No intervention test (e.g. masking nuisance regions at deployment or training to lower NMR) to show the relation is causal for generalization.
one_line: A masking-based visual attribution score for pi0.5 is more faithful than attention or token-norm maps, and tasks where it puts more weight on background and other nuisance regions have lower success (r = -0.77 on AGNOSTOS).
